checks.reason: The variational definition ranges over every smooth positive Gauduchon metric. Every lower comparison is established for each such metric before infima are taken.
A global L1 logarithmic potential pairs with dd^c of the smooth test; that derivative is zero by the Gauduchon condition.
Compactness gives c_h Omega<=h<=C_h Omega, so the current comparison applies to theta+epsilon h with fixed min/max constants.
Nef theta and positive perturbation have smooth positive representatives. B+epsilon Omega is positive, so the compared root volumes are positive.
The quotient comparison uses no constant-rank assumption; this exact part is carried to arbitrary Kähler modification sources.
A smooth semipositive constant-rank B on compact X has its R positive Omega-eigenvalues uniformly bounded above and away from zero.
The remaining n-R eigenvalues become epsilon and the positive ones become lambda+epsilon; relative to positive smooth mu this gives fixed two-sided epsilon^(n-R) density bounds.
Matrix AMGM in the wedge normalization has no extra n factor. Integrating the pointwise lower density gives lambda>=l^(1/n)epsilon^((n-R)/n).
The positive closed A_epsilon=B+epsilon Omega is itself Gauduchon, including n=1.
Writing A_epsilon^n=f_epsilon mu gives integral f_epsilon^((n-1)/n)mu and the stated exponent. Dividing yields epsilon^((n-R)/n).
At R=0 the same computation applies; at n=1 the denominator is one. No active-block minimum is taken over an empty set.
Raising positive quotient bounds to n and dividing logarithms by log epsilon gives the common order n-R, independent of the chosen smooth data.
In t_j=1 coordinates w_a=t_a w_j are the standard charts of the linear-center blowup. They cover the incidence variety and show smoothness.
Writing w=lambda t makes q a locally trivial projective (ell+1)-space bundle; hence q is a submersion and Q has constant rank r=m-ell-1>=1.
The incidence variety is embedded in the product of projective spaces; H+Q is the restriction of its positive product Fubini--Study form.
The coordinate section w_j factors as lambda t_j and has divisor E+q-pullback of its hyperplane. Thus O(E)=p*O(1) tensor q*O(-1).
The accepted divisor curvature convention yields dd^c psi_E=[E]-H+Q with locally integrable squared logarithms and multiplicity one along smooth E.
Adding half that logarithm makes H at least (H+Q)/2 and leaves a positive E/2 current.
All parameters are nonnegative, fixed f_i/g_i strictly positive and H_i/Q_i semipositive; every cone member is semipositive and its positive Hermitian perturbation needs no potential.
On every active block the corresponding a+b f or c+d g has a strictly positive uniform minimum. Inactive blocks are identically zero.
B_theta uses kappa_i for H-active blocks, Q_i for Q-only blocks and zero otherwise. The product block rank is exactly sum R_i.
Uniform coefficient bounds and H_i,Q_i<=kappa_i give theta<=C B_theta, with absent H terms on Q-only blocks.
Subtract the constant minimum u_i from each H coefficient, add (u_i/2)psi_E and retain nonnegative smooth remainders. Plain/Q-only active minima complete the lower bound.
Theta=0 has B=0 and phi=0, so the comparison holds with any positive c. Its exponent is n.
Constants are fixed for the chosen background, coefficients, probability and metric; no uniform constant across all parameter faces is asserted.
A positive small bump varying in a q-fiber has dg wedge Q nonzero because r>=1. Activating it alone prevents cancellation; cross-factor variation gives nonclosed fH1 on Pp times Pq.
Adding dd^c of a smooth real function does not change the exterior derivative of the background.
Pulling back old fixed functions sets the new Q coefficients to zero. Each active plain H becomes an active blown H with effective rank m, so the total rank and bounds are preserved.
For a surjective modification every nonzero divisor section remains nonzero. Its pulled-back holomorphic squared logarithm is locally integrable; no general L1 pullback theorem is used.
Pull back only explicit smooth nonnegative remainders and section curvature identities, giving positive effective divisors upstairs and the rank-free sandwich.

checks.reason: Pullback cannot increase rank, so (pi*B)^(R+1)=0. On the nonempty isomorphism locus rank is R and its Rth wedge against a Kähler metric has positive integral.
The accepted dual smooth equation and closed Stokes formula give V(pi*B+epsilon OmegaY)=its top intersection for each positive epsilon and any smooth positive probability on Y.

That top intersection is a finite polynomial with nonnegative coefficients, a positive coefficient at k=R and no k>R. For epsilon<=1 it is bounded above and below by fixed multiples of epsilon^(n-R). This strengthens the author order-only extension.
The upstairs probability is separately chosen smooth and positive; a vanishing pullback of the downstairs probability is never inserted into the dual formula.

Integer tensor powers, including negative powers, carry the fixed product metrics. Finite nonnegative real combinations give curvature eta_D and an actual effective current through the accepted global squared-log identity.

A point where a section is nonzero exists outside the exceptional divisors. Restriction to a fiber projective line through that point remains nonzero and has degrees H=1,Q=0, forcing its H exponent nonnegative.
Choose A with Aw=z at that point. The projective section [t]->([At:t],[t]) contains it and has H=Q=1 on a projective line, so the sum of exponents is nonnegative.
Positive real sums preserve both inequalities; conversely delta E+(delta+rho)F_Q realizes every allowed blown pair and plain hyperplanes realize every plain coefficient.
a>=delta and c>=rho make the explicitly displayed residual parameters nonnegative, hence preserve semipositivity and nefness; they are only sufficient conditions for this representation.
(theta-beta)+dd^c Phi_D=[D]>=0 is the precise positive-current subtraction premise, with the fixed curvature representative retained.
If initial H is absent, a=b=0 and the divisor/residual inequalities force delta=0,rho>=0, preventing Q gain. If H disappears its rank drops from m to r<m or zero.
Apply n-R on both backgrounds; all block losses are nonnegative and cannot cancel. Equality is exactly retention of each initially leading H or Q-only generator.
For theta_t=tH+gQ, positivity follows from a kappa lower bound. Removing sE leaves (t-s)H+(g+s)Q; leading rank stays m for s<t and becomes r at s=t. The exterior derivative stays dg wedge Q.
All smooth semipositive residuals admit smooth positive perturbations, so perturbative minimal divisorial multiplicities vanish even when a chosen boundary current has actual t[E].

Fixed f/g must be strictly positive; zero parameters and zero background are included. Unrestricted residual cones, vanishing fixed functions and non-Kähler sources are excluded. General P02 remains open; no MA mass-extremum claim or generated model verdict is used.
